text:
Git branching is a powerful feature that helps developers work on new features without disrupting the main codebase. Instead of making changes directly to the main branch, you create a separate feature branch. This branch is like a copy of the project where you can experiment freely.

Once your work is ready, you can merge it back into the main branch. Before merging, many teams use pull requests. A pull request is a formal way to review code, discuss changes, and ensure everything works well. This review process catches mistakes and improves code quality.

Overall, a good version control workflow with branches keeps your project organized, reduces conflicts, and allows multiple people to collaborate safely.
